kayitlar.title: Tracking GitHub repository releases with the REST API and webhooks
kayitlar.summary: How to read a repository's releases through the GitHub REST API, page through them, accept release webhooks safely, and combine webhooks with polling so missed or repeated deliveries do not corrupt tracked state.
kayitlar.short_answer: List releases with GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases and follow the link header until no rel="next" remains; per_page is capped at 100 and larger values are silently reduced. Drafts appear only for users with push access, and "latest" is ordered by commit date. For webhooks, verify X-Hub-Signature-256 with a constant-time comparison, answer 2XX within 10 seconds, deduplicate on X-GitHub-Delivery, and redeliver missed deliveries yourself within 3 days, since GitHub does not retry automatically.

claims.text: The list releases endpoint does not return Git tags that have no associated release.
claims.quote: This returns a list of releases, which does not include regular Git tags that have not been associated with a release.

claims.text: Draft releases are listed only for users who have push access to the repository.
claims.quote: Information about published releases are available to everyone. Only users with push access will receive listings for draft releases.

claims.text: For the list releases endpoint, per_page has a maximum of 100 and a default of 30.
claims.quote: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API." Default: 30

claims.text: The "latest" release is the newest non-draft, non-prerelease release ordered by created_at, which is the commit date rather than the publish date.
claims.quote: The latest release is the most recent non-prerelease, non-draft release, sorted by the created_at attribute. The created_at attribute is the date of the commit used for the release, and not the date when the release was drafted or published.

claims.text: A paginated response carries a link header, and the header is absent when all results fit on one page or the endpoint is not paginated.
claims.quote: When a response is paginated, the response headers will include a link header. If the endpoint does not support pagination, or if all results fit on a single page, the link header will be omitted.

claims.text: A per_page value above the maximum is reduced to the maximum without an error.
claims.quote: If you specify a value greater than the maximum, GitHub does not return an error. Instead, the value is automatically reduced to the maximum

claims.text: Each webhook delivery carries a hash signature in the X-Hub-Signature-256 header.
claims.quote: The hash signature will appear in each delivery as the value of the X-Hub-Signature-256 header.

claims.text: The signature should be compared with a constant-time comparison, not a plain equality operator.
claims.quote: Never use a plain == operator. Instead consider using a method like secure_compare or crypto.timingSafeEqual, which performs a "constant time" string comparison

claims.text: GitHub treats a delivery as failed when the receiver does not return a 2XX response within 10 seconds.
claims.quote: Your server should respond with a 2XX response within 10 seconds of receiving a webhook delivery. If your server takes longer than that to respond, then GitHub terminates the connection and considers the delivery a failure.

claims.text: The event type is given by the X-GitHub-Event header and the action by the top-level action key of the payload.
claims.quote: To determine the event type, you can use the X-GitHub-Event request header. To determine the action type, you can use the top-level action key in the event payload.

claims.text: GitHub does not retry failed deliveries on its own, and deliveries can be redelivered only for the past 3 days.
claims.quote: You can redeliver webhook deliveries that occurred in the past 3 days. GitHub does not automatically redeliver failed deliveries.

claims.text: A redelivered webhook keeps the X-GitHub-Delivery value of the original delivery.
claims.quote: If you request a redelivery, the X-GitHub-Delivery header will be the same as in the original delivery.

recommendations: Recommendation / inference: acknowledge a delivery once its signature checks out, queue the payload, and process it afterwards, to stay inside the 10-second window.
Recommendation / inference: store processed X-GitHub-Delivery values and skip repeats; since a redelivery reuses the original value, this also absorbs your own redeliveries.
Recommendation / inference: key tracked state on the release id, so the same release seen by webhook and by poll merges into one record.
Recommendation / inference: run a periodic reconciliation poll as a safety net for outages longer than the 3-day redelivery window.
not_covered: The release webhook payload and its action values (that reference was outside the permitted sources).

kayitlar.applies_to: GitHub REST API (releases and pagination; examples in the documents send X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10) and GitHub webhooks, as documented for github.com on docs.github.com/en.
